claims.claim: Anthropic defines workflows as systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths.
Anthropic defines agents as systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks.
OpenAI defines agents as systems that independently accomplish tasks on your behalf.
AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens frames orchestration patterns as a spectrum from static workflows to dynamic graph orchestration.
12-Factor Agents recommends owning control flow by keeping if/while logic in code while letting the model choose actions.
Anthropic recommends finding the simplest solution possible and only increasing complexity when needed.
Google Cloud Architecture Center publishes a 3-step selection process for agentic AI design patterns.
Cognition's 2026 revision states multi-agent works in a narrow class where one main loop carries state and subagents are stateless workers with narrow scope.
Anthropic reports that agents use approximately 4x more tokens than a chat interaction.
Anthropic reports that multi-agent systems use approximately 15x more tokens than a chat interaction.
A Claude Opus 4 lead agent with Claude Sonnet 4 subagents outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2% on Anthropic's internal research eval.
McKinsey estimates that agentic tasks can consume roughly 1,000x more tokens than single-turn reasoning/chat.
Anthropic identifies failure classes in emerging multiagent systems including conformity, epistemic failures, and incompatible goals.
Anthropic defines prompt chaining as decomposing a task into a sequence of steps where each LLM call processes the output of the previous one.
AWS describes prompt chaining as breaking complex tasks into sequential LLM steps enabling structured reasoning and control.
Google ADK's SequentialAgent executes its sub-agents in the order they are specified in a list.
AWS Prescriptive Guidance documents a prompt chaining saga pattern involving compensating transactions for multi-step writes.
Anthropic defines routing as classifying an input and directing it to a specialised follow-up task or handler.
AWS Well-Architected best practice AGENTCOST02 assigns routine classification and formatting to cost-efficient models and reserves premium models for reasoning.
OpenAI's guardrail taxonomy includes a relevance classifier that flags off-topic queries as a first-class guardrail layer.
Anthropic defines parallelization sectioning as breaking a task into independent subtasks run in parallel.
Anthropic defines parallelization voting as running the same task multiple times to get diverse samples.
Google ADK's ParallelAgent runs sub-agents concurrently potentially reducing total research time significantly compared to sequential execution.
In Google ADK, all parallel children access the same shared session.state.
LLMCompiler reports latency speedup up to 3.7x, cost savings up to 6.7x, and accuracy improvement of ~9% vs ReAct.
Anthropic's research system reported up to 90% reduction in research time on complex queries using 3-5 parallel subagents making 3+ parallel tool calls (confirmed only in secondary summaries).
Anthropic defines orchestrator-workers as a workflow where a central LLM dynamically breaks down tasks, delegates them to worker LLMs, and synthesizes their results.
Google Cloud defines hierarchical task decomposition as an implementation of the coordinator pattern where a top-level parent agent receives a task and decomposes it.
Microsoft Agent Framework supports magentic plan review via .with_plan_review() or MagenticHumanInterventionKind.PLAN_REVIEW.
Anthropic defines evaluator-optimizer as a workflow where one LLM call generates a response while another provides evaluation and feedback in a loop.
Google Cloud splits evaluator-optimizer into two named patterns: review and critique, and iterative refinement.
Microsoft Azure defines maker-checker loop as one agent creating or proposing something and another agent checking it, explicitly stating it is a specific type of group chat orchestration.
Google ADK's LoopAgent repeatedly executes its sub-agents for a specified number of iterations or until a termination condition is met.
Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals and maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer.
MAST classifies multi-agent failures into specification issues, inter-agent misalignment, and task verification categories.
The MAST study reports failure distribution as specification ~41.8%, inter-agent misalignment ~36.9%, and task verification ~21.3% (secondary-only source).
The OpenReview record for MAST notes the extended taxonomy has 16 modes across three categories.
The NeurIPS record for MAST notes the taxonomy has 14 modes.
OpenAI defines decentralized handoff pattern as agents handing off workflow execution to one another.
Azure lists infinite handoff loops as a risk in handoff orchestration.
Google ADK implements handoffs as the LLM emitting a transfer_to_agent function call.
OpenAI defines the manager pattern as a manager agent coordinating specialist agents where agents serve as tools for other agents.
Google Cloud defines the swarm pattern as using a dispatcher agent to route a user request to a collaborative group of specialized agents.
LangChain's handoff design requires choosing a context filtering strategy regarding conversation history.
AWS Well-Architected includes a best practice 'Optimize multi-agent collaboration cost through efficient handoff patterns'.
Microsoft Agent Framework allows agents in a handoff workflow to use tools that require human approval before they run.
Azure defines group chat orchestration as a collaborative conversation among multiple agents coordinated by an orchestrator determining speaker selection.
AutoGen's group chat manager keeps issuing RequestToSpeak until a termination condition is reached.
Academic multiagent debate involves multiple model instances proposing answers, reading each other's responses, and revising over rounds.
Azure defines magentic orchestration as also known as dynamic orchestration, task-ledger-based orchestration, or adaptive planning.
Magentic-One paper describes an Orchestrator agent creating a plan, delegating tasks, and tracking progress towards the goal with dynamic replanning.
Magentic-One uses an outer loop for the Task Ledger and an inner loop for the Progress Ledger.
AutoGen documentation states that without a termination condition, the group chat will run indefinitely.
Microsoft Agent Framework magentic builder allows a reviewer to approve, request revisions, or reject the plan.
Google Cloud defines the human-in-the-loop pattern as improving safety and reliability by inserting human judgment into critical decision points within the workflow.
LangChain HITL middleware supports approve, edit, and reject with feedback actions.
LangGraph saves graph state using its persistence layer and waits indefinitely until execution is resumed when an interrupt is triggered.
Temporal provides Durable Execution allowing a Workflow to resume automatically after a crash, network timeout, or multi-day wait for a human approval.
AWS Well-Architected recommends Risk-tiered approval matching the level of human review to the risk and reversibility of each agent action.
AWS ambient agents expose notify, question, and review HITL patterns surfaced through an ask_human tool.
Agentic RAG survey defines architectures including single-agent (router), multi-agent, hierarchical, corrective (CRAG), adaptive, and graph-based RAG.
LangChain implements ideas from Self-RAG and CRAG using document grading and query rewriting loops.
LangChain defines ambient agents as agents that respond to signals and run tasks simultaneously, triggered by events rather than a human prompt.
AWS notes that AWS Step Functions can orchestrate workflows but cannot reason.
Anthropic's long-running harness pattern uses an initializer agent that writes a feature list/state file plus an incremental worker agent that makes progress across many context windows.
Gemini Deep Research agent autonomously plans, executes, and synthesizes multi-step research tasks to produce detailed, cited reports.
OpenAI's Deep Research was trained using end-to-end reinforcement learning on hard browsing and reasoning tasks.
Anthropic's Research feature uses tools to create parallel agents that search and read, requiring flexibility to pivot or explore tangential connections.
Deep research products allow users to edit the research plan before execution.
ReAct papers define agents generating both reasoning traces and task-specific actions in an interleaved manner.
OpenAI Agents SDK runner handles the agent loop and handoffs.
Anthropic reports that tool definitions and results can sometimes consume 50,000+ tokens before work starts.
Plan-and-Solve prompting divides the entire task into smaller subtasks via a plan, then carries out the subtasks according to the plan.
LLMCompiler variant generates a DAG of tasks with inter-dependencies dispatched by a Task Fetching Unit.
LangChain's Deep Agents harness productises the planner as a write_todos-style planning tool plus a virtual filesystem and subagent spawning.
Anthropic's multiagent research system mitigates delegation issues by teaching the orchestrator clear objective, output format, tool/source guidance and task boundaries.
Anthropic recommends scaling effort to query complexity to prevent agents from misjudging how many workers a query deserves.
Anthropic recommends starting wide then narrowing down because agents default to too-narrow searches.
AWS Prescriptive Guidance defines evaluator reflect-refine loops where feedback is applied by reinvoking the generator with an embedded critique or sending feedback to a specialized refiner.
No hyperscaler or model lab publishes a complete cross-pattern decision tree (unconfirmed absence).
Machine Learning Mastery publishes a decision-tree approach for choosing agentic design patterns.
Anthropic suggests developers start by using LLM APIs directly as many patterns can be implemented in a few lines of code.
OpenAI guide states a single agent can handle many tasks by incrementally adding tools, keeping complexity manageable.
Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework criteria for single agents include well-defined problem domains with predictable workflows.
Cognition blog 'Don't Build Multi-Agents' serves as a counter-position to premature multi-agent adoption.
AWS Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens includes a cost pillar with best practices for tiered model selection.
Google Cloud Architecture Center provides per-pattern cost notes in its design pattern catalogue.
Anthropic's effective context engineering page discusses compaction, note-taking, and sub-agents for managing finite attention budget.
Anthropic recommends just-in-time retrieval of identifiers rather than bulk preloading to protect context window.
OpenAI Agents SDK docs describe needs_approval interruptions that must be resumed.
Microsoft Agent Framework gates function tools requiring approval.
AWS Prescriptive Guidance maps agent patterns to AWS services including Bedrock, Lambda, Step Functions and EventBridge.
GitHub sample repo exists for building ambient agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Paper 'Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems' is attributed to Anthropic and reported as published ~2026-08-13 (secondary-only date confirmation).
Cognition's follow-up on multi-agents working is dated 2026-04-22.
Report confirms no contradiction with facts verified on 2026-10-31 about Alibaba Cloud Model Studio / AgentRun / AgentLoop.
Report states nothing in this brief touches Alibaba Cloud products.
LangGraph restates the workflow vs agent split defining workflows as having predetermined code paths.
Anthropic trade rule states agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance.
Anthropic states optimizing single LLM calls with retrieval and in-context examples is usually enough for many applications.
Anthropic states agents are used for open-ended problems where required number of steps is difficult or impossible to predict.
OpenAI defines a workflow as a sequence of steps that must be executed to meet the user's goal.
12-Factor Agents factor 'Contact humans with tool calls' is recommended for escalation.
Google Cloud selection process starts from requirements like task complexity, latency expectations, cost budget, and need for human involvement.
AWS names multiplicative overhead in multi-agent coordination due to reasoning cycles.
Google Cloud states coordinator pattern results in more model calls than a single-agent system.
Anthropic's implicit ladder goes from augmented LLM to workflow patterns to autonomous agents.
Suggested tree indicates prompt chaining applies when steps are linear and each step needs the previous.
Suggested tree indicates routing applies for distinct input categories.
Suggested tree indicates parallelization applies for independent subtasks or consensus needs.
Suggested tree indicates orchestrator-workers applies when subtasks are not known until runtime.
Suggested tree indicates evaluator-optimizer applies when clear eval criteria exist and refinement pays.
Suggested tree indicates ReAct tool loop applies when steps are unknown and model must decide path.
Suggested tree indicates plan-and-execute applies for long horizon, many tools, or cost-sensitive tasks.
Suggested tree indicates subagents under ONE stateful loop apply when one context cannot hold the task.
Suggested tree indicates group chat or debate applies when peers need to challenge each other.
Suggested tree indicates handoffs or swarm apply when a specialist emerges mid-conversation.
Suggested tree indicates magentic applies when no known recipe exists and planning/replanning is needed.
Suggested tree indicates agentic RAG applies when grounding is needed.
Suggested tree indicates event-driven durable execution applies for tasks triggered by events/schedules that are long-running.
